title: The Emperor’s Mirror: Wei Zheng
synopsis: How does Wei Zheng go from plotting the Emperor’s death to being his right-hand man?

fullText.simplified:
唐太宗的镜子—魏征

    唐太宗李世民在位期间，非常注重选拔人才，也非常善于听取别人的意见。关于他知人善用的故事有很多，其中最为后来人所知的就是他和大臣魏征的故事。
    魏征原本是唐太宗大哥李建成的谋士，曾经帮着李建成设计圈套想害死唐太宗。但事后，唐太宗毫不记仇，觉得魏征是个人才，照旧重用了他。有很多跟随唐太宗东征西讨的将士们不服气，认为魏征是“外人”，不应该重用。唐太宗向大家解释道：“我只从才干选择人，没有什么‘自己人’和‘外人’的差别，你们不要东想西想。”
    魏征为人正直，敢当面给唐太宗提意见，不会因为他是皇帝而给他留面子。唐太宗也会虚心听取魏征的意见，只要魏征说得有道理，他就会认真改正。
    唐太宗毕竟是皇帝，周围拍马屁的人很多，也会比较要面子。有时候魏征说到唐太宗的痛处，唐太宗气得跳起来要杀他，魏征依旧坚持自己的意见不变。等唐太宗冷静下来，觉得魏征说得对，只好老老实实向魏征认错。
    有一次，唐太宗外出考察，路过一个地方，因为伙食不好而大发脾气，把旁边的官员们都吓坏了。魏征却不怕，他毫不客气地对唐太宗说：“以前隋朝的皇帝就是像你这样挑三拣四，乱发皇帝脾气，所以隋朝灭亡了。你不吸取教训，这样乱发脾气干什么？”唐太宗认为魏征说得对，一下子就没了脾气。
    唐太宗对魏征又爱又恨，既喜欢他，又怕他。他把魏征称为“人镜”，还把魏征指出自己的十个缺点规规矩矩地贴在墙上，每天早晚认真看一遍，检查自己是不是又犯了老毛病。
    魏征死后，唐太宗大哭。他很伤心地对大家说：“人们以青铜做镜子，可以端正衣冠；用历史做镜子，可以知道国家兴衰的规律；用正直敢说话的人做镜子，可以知道自己什么事情做对了，什么事情做错了。现在魏征死了，我失去了一面多好的镜子啊！”
    直到现在，唐太宗和魏征的故事还是被当成佳话被人们传颂。没有魏征，唐太宗就听不见批评的声音；没有唐太宗这样开明的皇帝，魏征再说什么也没有用。弄不好，还可能丢掉自己的脑袋。所以，唐太宗离不开魏征，魏征也离不开唐太宗。正是因为唐太宗的开明和魏征的直言敢谏，成就了举世闻名的唐朝盛世！
fullText.traditional:
唐太宗的鏡子—魏徵

    唐太宗李世民在位期間，非常注重選拔人才，也非常善於聽取別人的意見。關於他知人善用的故事有很多，其中最為後來人所知的就是他和大臣魏徵的故事。
    魏徵原本是唐太宗大哥李建成的謀士，曾經幫著李建成設計圈套想害死唐太宗。但事後，唐太宗毫不記仇，覺得魏徵是個人才，照舊重用了他。有很多跟隨唐太宗東征西討的將士們不服氣，認為魏徵是“外人”，不應該重用。唐太宗向大家解釋道：“我只從才幹選擇人，沒有什麼‘自己人’和‘外人’的差別，你們不要東想西想。”
    魏徵為人正直，敢當面給唐太宗提意見，不會因為他是皇帝而給他留面子。唐太宗也會虛心聽取魏徵的意見，只要魏徵說得有道理，他就會認真改正。
    唐太宗畢竟是皇帝，周圍拍馬屁的人很多，也會比較要面子。有時候魏徵說到唐太宗的痛處，唐太宗氣得跳起來要殺他，魏徵依舊堅持自己的意見不變。等唐太宗冷靜下來，覺得魏徵說得對，只好老老實實向魏徵認錯。
    有一次，唐太宗外出考察，路過一個地方，因為伙食不好而大發脾氣，把旁邊的官員們都嚇壞了。魏徵卻不怕，他毫不客氣地對唐太宗說：“以前隋朝的皇帝就是像你這樣挑三揀四，亂發皇帝脾氣，所以隋朝滅亡了。你不吸取教訓，這樣亂發脾氣幹什麼？”唐太宗認為魏徵說得對，一下子就沒了脾氣。
    唐太宗對魏徵又愛又恨，既喜歡他，又怕他。他把魏徵稱為“人鏡”，還把魏徵指出自己的十個缺點規規矩矩地貼在牆上，每天早晚認真看一遍，檢查自己是不是又犯了老毛病。
    魏徵死後，唐太宗大哭。他很傷心地對大家說：“人們以青銅做鏡子，可以端正衣冠；用歷史做鏡子，可以知道國家興衰的規律；用正直敢說話的人做鏡子，可以知道自己什麼事情做對了，什麼事情做錯了。現在魏徵死了，我失去了一面多好的鏡子啊！”
    直到現在，唐太宗和魏徵的故事還是被當成佳話被人們傳頌。沒有魏徵，唐太宗就聽不見批評的聲音；沒有唐太宗這樣開明的皇帝，魏徵再說什麼也沒有用。弄不好，還可能丟掉自己的腦袋。所以，唐太宗離不開魏徵，魏徵也離不開唐太宗。正是因為唐太宗的開明和魏徵的直言敢諫，成就了舉世聞名的唐朝盛世！

sentences.simplified: 用正直敢说话的人做镜子，可以知道自己什么事情做对了，什么事情做错了。
sentences.traditional: 用正直敢說話的人做鏡子，可以知道自己什麼事情做對了，什麼事情做錯了。
sentences.pinyin: yòng zhèng zhí gǎn shuō huà de rén zuò jìng zi kě yǐ zhī dào zì jǐ shén me shì qing zuò duì le shén me shì qing zuò cuò le
sentences.english: Using history as a mirror, they can find out the patterns behind the rise and fall of a state.

sentences.simplified: 现在魏征死了，我失去了一面多好的镜子啊！”
sentences.traditional: 現在魏徵死了，我失去了一面多好的鏡子啊！”
sentences.pinyin: xiàn zài wèi zhēng sǐ le wǒ shī qù le yí miàn duō hǎo de jìng zi a
sentences.english: Using an honest, outspoken person as a mirror, they can know what they did right and what they did wrong.
Now that Wei Zheng has passed away, what a great mirror I have lost!

sentences.simplified: 直到现在，唐太宗和魏征的故事还是被当成佳话被人们传颂。
sentences.traditional: 直到現在，唐太宗和魏徵的故事還是被當成佳話被人們傳頌。
sentences.pinyin: zhí dào xiàn zài táng tài zōng hé wèi zhēng de gù shi hái shi bèi dàng chéng jiā huà bèi rén men chuán sòng

sentences.simplified: 没有魏征，唐太宗就听不见批评的声音；
sentences.traditional: 沒有魏徵，唐太宗就聽不見批評的聲音；
sentences.pinyin: méi yǒu wèi zhēng táng tài zōng jiù tīng bu jiàn pī píng de shēng yīn
sentences.english: To this day, the story of Emperor Taizong of Tang and Wei Zheng’s is a much-told tale and has spread far and wide.

sentences.simplified: 没有唐太宗这样开明的皇帝，魏征再说什么也没有用。
sentences.traditional: 沒有唐太宗這樣開明的皇帝，魏徵再說什麼也沒有用。
sentences.pinyin: méi yǒu táng tài zōng zhè yàng kāi míng de huáng dì wèi zhēng zài shuō shén me yě méi yǒu yòng
sentences.english: Without Wei Zheng, Emperor Taizong of Tang wouldn’t have heard the voices of criticism.

sentences.simplified: 弄不好，还可能丢掉自己的脑袋。
sentences.traditional: 弄不好，還可能丟掉自己的腦袋。
sentences.pinyin: nòng bù hǎo hái kě néng diū diào zì jǐ de nǎo dài
sentences.english: Without an emperor as open-minded as Emperor Taizong of Tang, anything Wei Zheng said would have been useless.

sentences.simplified: 所以，唐太宗离不开魏征，魏征也离不开唐太宗。
sentences.traditional: 所以，唐太宗離不開魏徵，魏徵也離不開唐太宗。
sentences.pinyin: suǒ yǐ táng tài zōng lí bù kāi wèi zhēng wèi zhēng yě lí bù kāi táng tài zōng
sentences.english: In a bad scenario, he might have lost his head.

sentences.simplified: 正是因为唐太宗的开明和魏征的直言敢谏，
sentences.traditional: 正是因為唐太宗的開明和魏徵的直言敢諫，
sentences.pinyin: zhèng shì yīn wèi táng tài zōng de kāi míng hé wèi zhēng de zhí yán gǎn jiàn
sentences.english: So, Emperor Taizong of Tang needed Wei Zheng, and Wei Zheng needed Emperor Taizong of Tang.

sentences.simplified: 成就了举世闻名的唐朝盛世！
sentences.traditional: 成就了舉世聞名的唐朝盛世！
sentences.pinyin: chéng jiù le jǔ shì wén míng de táng cháo shèng shì
sentences.english: It’s precisely Emperor Taizong of Tang’s open-mindedness and Wei Zheng’s outspokenness ..
.. that achieved the world-famous prosperity of the Tang Dynasty!

sentence_translations: Emperor Taizong of Tang’s Mirror: Wei Zheng
When Emperor Taizong of Tang, Li Shimin, was on the throne, he placed great emphasis on selecting talented individuals.
He was also very good at listening to others’ opinions.
There are many stories about his ability to judge people and make good use of them.
Of these, the one that has become most well known by later generations is the story of him and minister Wei Zheng.
Wei Zheng was originally the strategist of Emperor Taizong of Tang’s eldest brother, Li Jiancheng.
He once assisted Li Jiancheng in designing a trap to kill Emperor Taizong of Tang.
But after this happened, Emperor Taizong of Tang did not hold any grudge whatsoever.
He thought Wei Zheng was a talented person, and as before, put him in an important position.
Many officers and soldiers who had been with Emperor Taizong of Tang through countless wars were unconvinced.
They viewed Wei Zheng as an “outsider” who shouldn’t be put in an important position.
Emperor Taizong of Tang explained to everyone, ..
.. “I pick people only for their abilities; there is no difference between so-called ‘our own people’ and ‘outsiders’.” Don’t overthink it.
Wei Zheng was an honest person, and he had the conviction to voice his opinions directly to Emperor Taizong of Tang’s face.
He wouldn’t hold back to save the emperor’s face just because he was the emperor.
Emperor Taizong of Tang would also humbly listen to Wei Zheng’s opinions.
As long as what Wei Zheng said had solid reasoning, he would earnestly make changes.
Emperor Taizong of Tang, after all, was the emperor.
Many people around him would flatter him, and he cared about what others thought of him.
Sometimes Wei Zheng’s words would touch a sore spot, ..
.. and Emperor Taizong of Tang would be so angry that he would jump up and want to kill Wei Zheng.
But Wei Zheng would nevertheless maintain his position, unwavering.
After Emperor Taizong of Tang calmed down, he would realize that Wei Zheng was right.
So, he would have no choice but honestly admit his mistakes to Wei Zheng.
Once, Emperor Taizong of Tang went away on an inspection trip.
At a place he passed by, he lost his temper because the food wasn’t up to standards, ..
.., terrifying the court officials next to him.
Yet, Wei Zheng was not afraid. Without any trace of courtesy he said to Emperor Taizong of Tang, ..
.. “In the past the emperor of the Sui Dynasty was picky like you and easily lost his temper.
So, the Sui Dynasty was destroyed. Why is it that haven’t you learned this lesson and also lose your temper easily?”
Emperor Taizong of Tang thought that Wei Zheng was right, and immediately his temper subsided.
Emperor Taizong of Tang both loved and hated Wei Zheng. He liked him, yet was afraid of him at the same time.
He called Wei Zheng a “human mirror”, and even posted  on the wall the ten flaws in his character that Wei Zheng had pointed out.
Every morning and every evening he would earnestly look at them, examining himself to see if he relapsed into any bad habits.
After Wei Zheng passed away, Emperor Taizong of Tang cried deeply.
In his grief, he said to everyone, ..
.. “When people use a bronze mirror, they can adjust their dress.
Using history as a mirror, they can find out the patterns behind the rise and fall of a state.
Using an honest, outspoken person as a mirror, they can know what they did right and what they did wrong.
Now that Wei Zheng has passed away, what a great mirror I have lost!
To this day, the story of Emperor Taizong of Tang and Wei Zheng’s is a much-told tale and has spread far and wide.
Without Wei Zheng, Emperor Taizong of Tang wouldn’t have heard the voices of criticism.
Without an emperor as open-minded as Emperor Taizong of Tang, anything Wei Zheng said would have been useless.
In a bad scenario, he might have lost his head.
So, Emperor Taizong of Tang needed Wei Zheng, and Wei Zheng needed Emperor Taizong of Tang.
It’s precisely Emperor Taizong of Tang’s open-mindedness and Wei Zheng’s outspokenness ..
.. that achieved the world-famous prosperity of the Tang Dynasty!
